lead.title: Undara Bio, a Barcelona spin-off of CNIO, Hospital del Mar and Banc de Sang i Teixits, raises a €4.15M seed led by Invivo Partners for a cell immunotherapy against glioblastoma
lead.deck: The round, led by Invivo Partners with the Institut Català de Finances and BStartup (Banco Sabadell), is meant to take the first candidate from the RiPPLE platform (Redirected Immune Potentiation through Programmable Living Effectors), built on Luis Álvarez-Vallina's research, towards the clinic: engineered immune cells that target the tumour while reawakening the patient's own anti-tumour immunity, to get around the tumour heterogeneity and immune escape that defeat conventional T-cell therapies. Glioblastoma, the most common primary brain tumour in adults, carries a median survival of 15 to 16 months; the company, led by Carolina Pola with Luis Paz-Ares as co-founder, is CNIO's fourth equity stake, and CNIO has licensed it a jointly owned patent.

milestone.title: Faron doses the first patient in BEXERA, its first randomised placebo-controlled study of bexmarilimab in higher-risk myelodysplastic syndromes
milestone.summary: Bexmarilimab is a humanised antibody against Clever-1, a receptor on immunosuppressive macrophages that is also expressed on malignant blasts in the bone marrow. The double-blind Phase 2b compares two doses (1 and 3 mg/kg) plus azacitidine against placebo plus azacitidine in around 90 treatment-naïve patients across the UK, the US and continental Europe; the first patient was dosed at King's College Hospital, London.
milestone.why: In the Phase 1/2 BEXMAB study, the combination produced a 45% complete remission rate in the frontline setting, lasting a median 16.1 months: BEXERA must confirm that signal against a true control arm and set the Phase 3 dose. For the Turku biotech, it is the decisive test of the 'reprogram the macrophages' thesis in a blood cancer where azacitidine alone hits a ceiling.

deal.thesis: The Lund biotech closed on November 27 the sale of all rights to mitazalimab, a CD40 agonist antibody, to US-based Biossil: $0.75M in cash, up to $108M in milestones and mid-single-digit royalties, with Biossil taking on all development, manufacturing and patent costs. The token entry price for a clinical asset shows how much of a buyer's market it is for cash-strapped biotechs: Alligator, which says its cash runs through December 31, 2027, now relies mostly on milestones and royalties from HLX22 (in Phase 3 at Henlius, data expected in the second half of 2027) and mitazalimab.

brefsEurope.title: Contera Pharma spins its RNA business out into a new company, Threepoint Therapeutics, open to outside investors
brefsEurope.summary: Owned, like Contera, by South Korea's Bukwang Pharmaceutical and led by Thomas Sager, Threepoint takes over the October 2025 collaboration with Lundbeck and a portfolio headed by CP-102, an antisense oligonucleotide for Canavan disease and its first programme expected in the clinic. Contera keeps CP-012, a bedtime levodopa-carbidopa tablet heading into Phase 2 (DAWN-PD) in Parkinson's disease.

brefsEurope.title: Cambridge opens a £20M national hub to validate human-based alternatives to animal models
brefsEurope.summary: Led by Matthias Zilbauer at the Cambridge Stem Cell Institute, with the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology and the Wellcome Sanger Institute, the hub opened on November 27 to validate organoids, advanced cell models and AI models (NAMs) and to build shared standards with regulators. The goal: cut the failure rate of more than 90% among drug candidates that enter clinical trials.

brefsEurope.title: EMA opens consultation on the criteria for the transferable exclusivity voucher for priority antibiotics
brefsEurope.summary: Created by the EU pharmaceutical reform, the voucher (TEV) adds 12 months of data protection to a product of the holder's choice; it will be requested in an initial marketing authorisation application once the provisions take effect, expected in December 2026. The CHMP draft requires an antimicrobial active against a multidrug-resistant organism, a significant clinical benefit and a new mechanism; comments are open until January 31, 2027.

brefsEurope.title: An EMA DARWIN EU study shows obesity has become the leading indication for GLP-1s in Europe
brefsEurope.summary: Across more than 1.6 million people who started a GLP-1 between 2015 and 2025, in 12 databases from ten countries, obesity became the most common indication in several populations from 2022, driven by semaglutide and tirzepatide; prescribing dips coincide with shortages reported since 2022. A real-world evidence base that will weigh on future filings from obesity challengers.

brefsEurope.title: Bavarian Nordic hires its new CFO, Allan Bødskov Andersen, from Topsoe
brefsEurope.summary: Currently CFO of clean-energy group Topsoe, previously CFO of DLF and 16 years at Ørsted, where he worked on its IPO, he will join by June 2027 at the latest to succeed Henrik Juuel. An outside-industry profile picked by new CEO Tarja Stenvall.

brefsEurope.title: Viral vector manufacturer OXB adds former Sensorion CEO Nawal Ouzren to its board
brefsEurope.summary: CEO of French hearing-loss biotech Sensorion from 2017 to 2026, and previously at Shire and Baxalta, she joins OXB's board as an independent non-executive director on January 4, 2027. The Oxford CDMO makes lentiviral, AAV, adenoviral and MVA vectors at sites in the UK, Lyon, Strasbourg and the US.

brefsEurope.title: Orexo closes its rights issue: SEK 175M gross, 69.2% subscribed and topped up by DNB
brefsEurope.summary: Launched at SEK 0.80 per share for about SEK 253M, the issue brings in about SEK 175M gross and SEK 145M net; DNB Bank, which underwrote about SEK 159M, had to take up 28% of the shares. Dilution of about 86% for shareholders who did not participate, a sign of how hard it is for listed Nordic biotechs to raise money.

brefsIntl.title: Uganda launches Africa's first trial of an mRNA vaccine against Bundibugyo ebolavirus, with Moderna
brefsIntl.summary: The Uganda Virus Research Institute is enrolling 224 healthy volunteers aged 1 to 65 in this Phase 1 safety and immunogenicity study, against the strain behind the outbreak in the DRC, for which no vaccine or treatment exists. A real-world test of how fast the mRNA platform can respond to an outbreak.

brefsIntl.title: FDA pushes back its decision on Vertex's povetacicept in IgA nephropathy by three months
brefsIntl.summary: Vertex's answer to a late-cycle information request was classed as a 'major amendment': the decision on this dual BAFF/APRIL inhibitor moves from November 30, 2026 to no later than February 28, 2027. A delay of the same length for this dual-target fusion protein, with the FDA saying only that it needs more review time.

word.definition: Macrophages, the immune system's 'clean-up' cells, that the tumour recruits and turns to its advantage to hold back the immune attack: biotechs aim to reprogram them so they fight the cancer again.

parts.label: Suppressive macrophage
parts.role: the pro-tumour 'M2-like' state that dampens T cells and helps the tumour grow

parts.label: Target receptor
parts.role: the molecular lever: Clever-1, CD47-SIRPα, CD40, LILRB or Toll-like receptors

parts.label: Reprogramming molecule
parts.role: often an antibody that blocks the suppressive signal or activates the macrophage

how.t: The tumour draws in monocytes from the blood, which mature on site into macrophages and take on an immunosuppressive profile.
An antibody hits a receptor on these macrophages, such as Clever-1 for bexmarilimab or SIRPα, the 'don't eat me' signal, for BI 765063.
Once reprogrammed, macrophages engulf more tumour cells, present their antigens and re-energise T cells, which is why they are combined with other treatments.

word.why: After PD-1 inhibitors, the myeloid microenvironment is one of immuno-oncology's big frontiers: a University of Turku review counts nearly 200 agents tested in more than 700 trials. But monotherapy efficacy remains rare, around 5% response rates for several molecules, and many programmes have been dropped: value will go to combinations, patient-selection biomarkers and more macrophage-specific targets. Alligator's sale of mitazalimab (CD40) for $0.75M in cash and the start of Faron's controlled Phase 2b show both sides of the market.

startups.name: Faron Pharmaceuticals
startups.use: Bexmarilimab, an anti-Clever-1 antibody that reprograms immunosuppressive macrophages; first patient dosed in November 2026 in the randomised Phase 2b BEXERA (higher-risk myelodysplastic syndromes, with azacitidine)

startups.name: Macomics
startups.use: University of Edinburgh spin-out developing macrophage-targeting antibodies; MACO-355, a pan-LILRB antibody that reprograms suppressive macrophages preclinically, described in 2024 as in CMC and IND-enabling studies

startups.name: OSE Immunotherapeutics
startups.use: BI 765063, an anti-SIRPα antibody that lifts the CD47-SIRPα 'don't eat me' signal to restore macrophage phagocytosis; in Phase 1 in advanced solid tumours, licensed to Boehringer Ingelheim
